= Vendored Rust crates

== liquid-core 0.26.11

This directory is derived from the official crates.io archive for
`liquid-core` 0.26.11. The archive SHA-256 is
`fc623edee8a618b4543e8e8505584f4847a4e51b805db1af6d9af0a3395d0d57`, verified
against the crates.io registry checksum before extraction. The path override in
the project lockfile has no registry checksum of its own.
The crate is licensed `MIT OR Apache-2.0`; the upstream license files and
copyright headers are retained.

The only source/dependency change replaces `anymap2` 0.13 with `anymap3` 1.1
in both Cargo manifests and in `src/runtime/runtime.rs`. The `Registers` type
continues to expose the same `get_mut<T: Any + Default>() -> RefMut<T>` API.
A focused test checks that register values persist and distinct types remain
separate. `anymap3` 1.1 is licensed `BlueOak-1.0.0 OR MIT OR Apache-2.0`, with
Rust 1.56 MSRV; this project uses its MIT or Apache-2.0 option.

The registry `Cargo.lock` was omitted because the root workspace lockfile is
authoritative. `.cargo_vcs_info.json` was omitted because it is registry
packaging metadata; the source archive hash above preserves provenance.
No archive links were present. Extraction rejected absolute paths, parent
traversal, and non-regular entries.

=== Maintenance and removal

This is a narrow downstream patch, not an upstream Liquid release. Keep the
base version at 0.26.11 and use a workspace `[patch.crates-io]` override for
this path. Revisit when Liquid publishes a release that replaces `anymap2`.
Then remove this directory and the override only after the all-features
dependency tree no longer includes the advisory and behavior checks pass.

== tree-sitter-language-pack 1.25.0

The base is the crates.io archive with SHA-256
`aeab6dd57fa75ca32f55a3160cce30a8d3217882260ae21c7527df2d41b50f2e`.
The MIT license file comes from the corresponding upstream commit
`ea44208da50de9a4d602bbc243d7a6949c4a2007`. The bundled utf8proc license
is included. The workspace lockfile replaces the packaged crate lockfile.

The Cargo override and exact dependency version keep Aden on this patch.
These settings apply to builds in this checkout. Cargo consumers that
resolve a published Aden crate apply patches from their own workspace root.
For a downloaded bundle, the build verifies the entire archive against the
upstream SHA-256 sidecar, extracts the selected grammar sources and keeps
query inputs for every language. After compiling and embedding, it deletes
the temporary inputs from Cargo's output directory. Local grammar sources
remain available for development, and Cargo watches external inputs for
changes. An unchanged build reuses Cargo's compiled output.

Remove this override when a compatible upstream release passes a cold and
repeated build with the default languages, embeds the same static grammars
and queries, and preserves offline inputs and grammar patch handling.

== rmcp 3.11.0

The base is the official crates.io archive, SHA-256
`391f153431ab68664d946513ea0cb3edbca78eaf99c5a983036cacab6220d85b`,
verified against the pre-patch workspace lockfile. The archive records
upstream revision `165f8fd514afb8f6d1be3e86260ee9abfce58541`.
The Apache-2.0 license is retained. The workspace lockfile is authoritative;
the nested lockfile and registry packaging provenance file were omitted.

The backport applies the date and duration changes from
https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk/pull/1474[RMCP PR 1474],
head `9043cdfa8694d83bf506c2f3eb0313ec173edd7e`.
It uses Jiff for internal clocks and wire formatting, with the published
Chrono annotation API available behind an optional feature. Aden disables
RMCP defaults and explicitly retains its stdio, server, base64, macro and
test-client features. It does not enable authentication features that could
independently bring in Chrono. `build = false` disables the archived RMCP
checkout hook installer in both manifests.

The RustSec workspace scan covers the resolved registry dependencies. Check
the underlying SDK's RustSec advisories separately while it is a local path
patch. On 2026-11-18 all four RMCP advisories in the database had fixes in or
before the 3.11.0 base. Remove this override when a compatible registry release
can omit Chrono and both Aden MCP entry points and the locked audit pass again.
